This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Ohio achieved statehood 1803 (17th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Underground Railroad; Civil War. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Ohio its number among the states.

title: The statehood story

definition: How Ohio went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Ohio: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Presidents; industry; aviation. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Ohio's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Columbus
d: Columbus is the capital of Ohio.
definition: Columbus is the capital of Ohio.
description: Columbus has been the seat of Ohio government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Ohio's largest is Columbus — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Buckeye State
description: The nickname "Buckeye State" captures how Ohio sees itself — and how America sees it. Seven U.S. presidents were born in Ohio. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "With God, all things are possible."
